content:
Without thinking today I wrote g '' f '' S for two functions f, g and a set S. I thought this would mean taking the image of S under f and then under g, i.e. g '' (f '' S). But actually it means (g '' f) '' S, i.e. take the image of f under g and then take the image of S under the resulting "function". (You can actually get it to typecheck, under sufficiently many free variables, since Set X = X -> Prop, and so I ended up with really weird errors like "this Set Nat is expected to be a Set Prop" and things like that.)

Would anyone ever intentionally write (g '' f) '' S? Shouldn't we just make this operator right-associative and prevent this mistake?
Same thing has bothered me with docs#Set.preimage for the longest time

Data point: according to the beautiful commands rg "''"' \(.*'"''" and rg "''"' .*\) '"''" the first syntax has 200 matches and the second has 68 matches, of which the majority on quick expection appear to be false positives. I'll make a PR.

• #38625 does the associativity change,
  • #38626 semi-automatedly removes a lot of superfluous parentheses.
